heuristics: H1 coverage: the 6N^2 distinct rationals a w/(u a' w') hit z like independent uniform elements of H (toy: 0.4025 at 400 trials and 0.3895 at 2000 trials vs 0.3935 predicted; standard error 0.011 cannot separate 0.4055 from 0.39, so production success rests on H1)
H2/H2' H-prime density 1/2^20 among primes and exponential gaps (list sizes and the 2^33 gap bound, checked when the lists are built)
H3 key bits: 192-bit parity y-keys behave as independent uniform strings across mu6 orbits (bucket occupancy, comparison and false-match caps; toy chi-square 31.32 vs 31)
limitations: Analytic bound; no full-size run. Instruction counts itemised, not measured on hardware.
Memory is exponential (2^123.3242 bytes, the exact itemised sum over all nodes at full allocation, asserted as an integer inequality; records alone 2^120.66).

Per-node comparison cap, per-slot cap, candidate caps at owner and generating nodes, re-walk cap and node overflow make the run fail with total probability below 2^-20 + 2^-40 under H1 and H3; every tail is rounded towards the larger probability; charged work is the maximum, not the expectation.

Depends on the walk-with-one-addition idea of cbadde77, the H-prime semiprime construction of 6ecec8e3 / cf6d45a8 and the bucket-matching package of 0a45ddb2; the one score change from that package is the per-node comparison cap, 1.003x instead of 1.01x the per-node mean (Bernstein tail below 2^-89); the preprocessing figure is upward-rounded and integer-asserted (pre^10000 <= 2^1157954).
